key_insight: PRIME adds a learned feedback loop to VLA driving models so early perception can be guided by downstream reasoning and navigation goals, rather than treating every visual cue equally. It uses situational memory embeddings to make perception more goal-aware and context-sensitive.
problem_solved: Existing Vision-Language-Action models are mostly feedforward: perception processes scenes without knowing what the planner or reasoner needs next. This paper addresses the gap between early visual encoding and high-level driving intent.
method: Introduces a learned feedback mechanism from reasoning/planning back into perception.
Stores situational context in memory embeddings to influence what the model attends to in future frames.
Integrates the feedback into VLA pipelines for autonomous driving so perception is conditioned on task-relevant cues.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical way to improve closed-loop decision making in embodied systems by making perception adaptive to goals. It may lead to more robust, efficient, and context-aware autonomous driving models.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing perception, reasoning, planning, and the new feedback loop into perception.

paper_title: PRIME: Perception Feedback with Situational Memory Embeddings in VLA Models
paper_authors: Erik Deinzer, Naya Baslan, Luca Paparusso, Narunas Vaskevicius, Peter Knott
